To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thioredoxins are important in the regeneration of oxidatively inactivated proteins in endothelial cells.
thioredoxins are involved in the regeneration in endothelial cells of proteins inactivated in vitro by oxidative stress.
thioredoxins and their reductases in mammalian cells are involved in the regeneration (repair) of proteins inactivated (denatured) by oxidative stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the thioredroxin/thioredoxine reductase system in cultured endothelial cell.
the identification, characterization, and regulation of proteins involved in the regeneration and/or protection of proteins from oxidative stress in endothelium.
the identification of a novel protein, thioredoxin.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
thioredoxins are the main proteins involved in the regeneration in the cell of oxidatively inactivated proteins, including those of the antioxidant enzymes.
the thioredoxins, which are ubiquitous in mammalian cells, play a crucial role in the regeneration of H2O2-damaged proteins in endothelial cells.
the thioredoxins are involved in the regeneration and protection of the enzymes in the endothelial cells against oxidative damage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thioredoxins in endothelial cells are in reduced form, and the thioredoxs are involved in the regeneration (repair) of the proteins inactivated by reactive oxygen species.
thioredoxins are the major redox-regulatory proteins in endothelial cells.
the thioredoxins are the main regenerative machinery for the inactivated proteins by the oxidative stress in endothelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thioredoxins are not only important for the antioxidant defense of the cell but also for the repair of proteins inactivated during oxidative stress.
we have shown that thioredoxins are involved in the repair of proteins inactivated in endothelial cells by H2O2.
thioredoxins are important in maintaining the integrity of the endothelium, the innermost lining of our blood vessels.
